title: Circus routes, pay and winter quarters
summary: The circus route took them to New Orleans and Baton Rouge; Joe made twenty-one dollars a week with two held back, and circuses wintered in places like Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So anyway, I looked in the... The Billboard showed the routes of all the different circuses, too, where they was going, and the dates. So I seen right smack there where Al G. Barnes was going to New Orleans and Baton Rouge.
They must have had a heck of a turnover if they advertised and showed the routes.
Oh, yes. But they were all just one-nighters.
And like I said, my ambition was to play on a circus parade in Baton Rouge. So anyway, I got on that, and soon enough I got to Baton Rouge...
So they went back to New Orleans when you joined them in Cincinnati.
Okay. Playing one-nighters going down to New Orleans.

I had quit the medicine show, you remember, in Harrisburg, and got into all that trouble, and I seen in the Billboard... When I had gotten in all that trouble, I had finished with being a gangster or whatever, or working for bootleggers. And I joined the circus. And I said to myself... And I didn't like it... After I got on it, I didn't like it. I said, 'When I get to Baton Rouge and play on this circus parade, then that's it.' You were only making $21 a week, and they held two dollars out of that every week. That was to keep you in the circus. Because too many guys worked a couple of weeks and jumped down. So they held out a part of your money until you got to winter quarters.
Oh, it was a seasonal thing, then.
Oh yes! And Al G. Barnes had winter quarters right here in Los Angeles. It was one of the big wild animal circuses, you see.
What's that circus down somewhere in Florida that's still got (?) down there?
That was the same kind of thing. They had a place that...
Same thing. All circuses had winter quarters, where they went for the winter.
And they owned that plot of land?

Oh yes, oh yes. Well, actually Ringling Brothers is your biggest circus. But they had all kinds of different places in winter quarters. At one time or another in the Twenties...no, from 1910 to 1918, West Baden, Indiana, about six of the big circuses used to have winter quarters there for some reason nobody knows. But in those days you had circuses like (?)Cell Sloto(?), John Robinson's Ten Big Shows, the Haidenbeck-Wallace Circus, and the Ringling Brothers, Barnum and Bailey. Barnum and Bailey was a single circus at one time. And I think Ringling and Barnum and Bailey combined in about 1920.
